prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Alder Creek Electrical Distribution Substation supplies approved-limit transformer/feeder circuits; observation cannot replace protection/control/field verification. Bay Automation Controller (Juniper): North Bay Controller/South Bay Controller retain distinct scopes; validate requests against mode/interlocks/authority/availability; execute approved ordered/hold/stop sequences; coordinate shared equipment; compare returned indications; flag incomplete/contradictory outcomes; associate Breaker Inspection Tag equipment/authorized-record context; degrade over-age points; send timestamped Bay Status Digest to Station Supervisory Control System (Glasswing). North blocks unready-interlock closing; maintains approved-mode local control during communications loss. South reports mode/control availability. Breaker Control Unit applies authorized/interlocked/permitted-mode outputs; returns position/circuit-health; local authority prevails. Glasswing presents authorized controls/indications, quality/staleness; produces Alarm Acknowledgement Slip; retains cleared history separately from current quality; verifies currency after recovery. Control Room Operator uses approved procedures/configured interface; reviews alarms/device/sequence/feeder/protection/DC before acknowledgement; records responses/outstanding actions; clearing proves no correction; discrepancies remain abnormal; produces Clearance Handoff Memo; verifies handback consistency before closure. Station Gateway brokers authorized traffic through configured mappings/addressing/access; rejects malformed/stale/unauthorized requests with review context; carries timestamped/quality-tagged indications; reports link/protocol faults without changing equipment state; produces Protocol Retry Summary. Layers remain independent during communications loss. Feeder Protection Relay (Tandem) independently trips using approved settings; produces Relay Diagnostic Note. North Protection Panel independently maintains feeder-zone logic/trip paths. Transformer Protection Panel independently protects transformer; locally indicates operations/reports abnormalities. Protection Relay Engineer (Larkspur) investigates/events/coordination; settings require independent approval, compatibility/installation/functional checks; discrepancies block release. Satellite Time Receiver (Bluefin) supplies quality-checked reference/holdover; sends Clock Drift Snapshot to Sequence Event Archive (Orchard): ordered outcomes/timestamps/uncertainty/corrections/history; auditable access/retention/holds/backups/recovery/faithful exports; timing quality cannot validate protection/measurement. Station DC System: monitored protection/control supply; loss abnormal; Battery Load Test Record. Engineering Workstation: revision/history review; Settings Review Receipt; not routine-command/immediate-assessment substitute. Maintenance Remote Terminal: authorized sessions/no interlock bypass. Substation Supervisor: authorization/escalation. Substation Field Crew (Cinder):

New part:
S195: Substation Supervisor ensures communication changes, point mapping changes, and control logic changes are managed through station change control.
S196: Substation Field Crew verifies equipment indications locally when remote status is uncertain and reports discrepancies through established operating channels.
S197: Maintenance windows are planned around feeder loading, switching constraints, and the availability of qualified personnel.
S198: The Substation Supervisor coordinates work timing with the Switching Desk Coordinator and confirms that operating responsibilities are understood.
S199: The Control Room Operator reviews the equipment affected by each work package and identifies any required operating restrictions.
S200: The Switching Desk Coordinator confirms switching prerequisites before field work begins and keeps the approved switching sequence current.
S201: Substation Field Crew performs work only after required clearances, isolation, and grounding have been confirmed through established procedures.
S202: Work boundaries are verified locally before personnel approach exposed conductors or operate equipment under maintenance.
S203: The Protection Relay Engineer reviews test scope, approved settings, and restoration criteria before protection testing starts.
S204: Testing is performed with approved procedures, calibrated instruments, and a defined means of stopping the test if unexpected indications occur.
S205: The Engineering Workstation is used for authorized configuration review, and changes are applied only through station change control.
S206: The Maintenance Remote Terminal uses the review receipt to support controlled maintenance review.
S207: The Bay Automation Controller uses the load test record to support maintenance review.
S208: The Station Supervisory Control System receives the Protocol Retry Summary for operational review.
S209: Cinder verifies that field work remains within the approved work boundary and reports any unsafe condition through established channels.
S210: Orchard retains event information needed to review testing and restoration activity.
S211: Feeder Protection Relay testing is coordinated so that protection coverage is not unintentionally removed from an energized feeder.
S212: A protection function placed out of service is tracked by the responsible operator until it is restored and verified.
S213: The Breaker Control Unit is tested using controlled commands that cannot bypass local interlocks or approved operating authority.
S214: Remote commands are inhibited when equipment status is uncertain or when required permissives are unavailable.
S215: If communications are degraded, the Control Room Operator treats remote indications as unavailable until their reliability is established.
S216: Substation Field Crew verifies equipment indications locally when remote status is uncertain and reports discrepancies through established operating channels.
S217: Manual operation is permitted only under approved procedures and with the required local checks and communication with the Control Room Operator.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
